latest_release.body:
# Highlighted changes

- Add Orderbook websocket support.
- Fully Decouple bot from RPC messaging for more reliable bot loop execution.
- Parameter values are now kept per strategy instance. Access them through `self.<param>.value`, not through the class.
- Armv7 (raspberry 32bit)  image updated to python 3.13.
- Dropped support for python 3.11.
- Support changing strategy parameters from Backtesting UI (`webserver` mode only).
- FreqUI will now use the backtested strategy to plot in backtest mode (`webserver` mode only).
- `backtesting-show --export-params` now writes the parameters from a backtest back to the strategy.
- Improved efficiency for `AgeFilter` doing fewer calls for validated pairs.

## Sponsor

You can sponsor the work on freqtrade via the following links:

- froggleston (FTUI) https://github.com/sponsors/froggleston/
- robcaulk (freqAI) https://github.com/sponsors/robcaulk/
- xmatthias (freqtrade and freqUI): https://github.com/sponsors/xmatthias/

## New Contributors
* @Siegelth made their first contribution in https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/pull/13657
* @Jhacarreiro made their first contribution in https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/pull/13662
* @Bortlesboat made their first contribution in https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/pull/13678
* @lizimu1013 made their first contribution in https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/pull/13697
* @louisvikk6-max made their first contribution in https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/pull/13681
* @M1ch43lV made their first contribution in https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/pull/13719

## How to update

As always, you can update your bot using one of the following commands:

### docker-compose

```bash
docker-compose pull
docker-compose up -d
```

### Installation via setup script

``` bash
# Deactivate venv and run 
./setup.sh --update
```

### Plain native installation

``` bash
git pull
pip install -U -r requirements.txt
```

# ![freqtrade](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/develop/docs/assets/freqtrade_poweredby.svg)

[![Freqtrade CI](https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=develop)](https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![DOI](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.04864/status.svg)](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.04864)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/freqtrade/freqtrade/branch/develop/graph/badge.svg?token=AD5BG3ATKI)](https://codecov.io/gh/freqtrade/freqtrade)
[![Documentation](https://readthedocs.org/projects/freqtrade/badge/)](https://www.freqtrade.io)
[![Discord Server](https://img.shields.io/badge/Freqtrade_Discord-4E4E4E?logo=discord)](https://discord.gg/p7nuUNVfP7)

Freqtrade is a free and open source crypto trading bot written in Python. It is designed to support all major exchanges and be controlled via Telegram or webUI. It contains backtesting, plotting and money management tools as well as strategy optimization by machine learning.

![freqtrade](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/develop/docs/assets/freqtrade-screenshot.png)

## Disclaimer

This software is for educational purposes only. Do not risk money which
you are afraid to lose. USE THE SOFTWARE AT YOUR OWN RISK. THE AUTHORS
AND ALL AFFILIATES ASSUME NO RESPONSIBILITY FOR YOUR TRADING RESULTS.

Always start by running a trading bot in Dry-Run and do not engage money
before you understand how it works and what profit/loss you should
expect.

We strongly recommend you to have coding and Python knowledge. Do not
hesitate to read the source code and understand the mechanism of this bot.
